policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'who met Abraham ... and blessed him' renders either the articular participle (ὁ συναντήσας) or the relative (ὃς συναντήσας) identically; English 'who met' does not distinguish them and no note is mapped here.

ASV reads 'unto whom Abraham, the patriarch, gave a tenth' with nothing rendering an adverbial καί; the ASV renders such a καί as 'even' (KJV here has 'to whom even the patriarch Abraham'), so its absence tracks the shorter ᾧ.
The variant is only the article before the proper name Ἀβραάμ; ASV 'hath taken tithes of Abraham' is the same English either way and no note is mapped here.
The variant is only the article before the proper name Μελχισέδεκ; ASV 'when Melchizedek met him' is the same English either way and no note is mapped here.

ASV 'for under it hath the people received the law' renders ἐπ' αὐτῆς, the genitive with ἐπί in its 'under/in the time of' sense; the dative ἐπ' αὐτῇ would give a basis or ground ('on it'), which the ASV wording does not express.
ASV 'hath the people received the law' is a perfect, matching the perfect νενομοθέτηται; the pluperfect νενομοθέτητο would have given 'had received'.
ASV 'Moses spake nothing concerning priests' has the plural noun 'priests' (ἱερέων); the RP reading has the abstract singular ἱερωσύνης, 'priesthood', which the ASV does not render.
σαρκίνης and σαρκικῆς are both rendered 'carnal'; ASV 'a carnal commandment' does not distinguish them, and the only note here is a greek_gloss on 'indissoluble' elsewhere in the verse.
ASV 'for it is witnessed of him' is passive, rendering μαρτυρεῖται; the active μαρτυρεῖ would give 'he testifieth/witnesseth'.

ASV ends the oath quotation at 'Thou art a priest for ever' with nothing rendering κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ, which the ASV renders explicitly wherever it stands (cf. 7:17 'After the order of Melchizedek').
τοσοῦτο and τοσοῦτον are orthographic variants of the same neuter form; ASV 'by so much' renders either and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'by so much also hath Jesus become the surety' renders an adverbial καί; nothing else in the verse accounts for 'also', so the ASV reflects καὶ κρείττονος.
ASV 'separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens' renders the conjunction καί before the participle; the RP omission would leave the two phrases asyndetic.
